# Official Evidence — KTH MSc Computer Science (Master's Programme in Computer Science), target Fall 2027

**Source URL:** https://www.kth.se/en/studies/master/computer-science/entry-requirements-computer-science-1.419975

**Note on source cycle:** The page does not explicitly state an application cycle/year (e.g., "Fall 2027"). The only dated figures it gives are for the **2026 admission** (acceptance-rate data below). No Fall 2027 admission-year statement is present on this page; that remains unknown from this source.

## Admission process (general)
- To be admitted, you must meet the admission requirements, submit all application documents, and pass the selection.
- "The same process applies to students with a bachelor's degree from a Swedish university."

## Bachelor's degree requirement
- Academic qualifications from an internationally recognised university equivalent to a Swedish bachelor's degree.
- You can meet the requirement if you are in the **final year** of your bachelor's studies.
- Students at universities **abroad** must submit documents according to the instructions from University Admissions.
- Students at **Swedish universities** must have completed **150 credits** in their programme **by 1 February**, per the instructions from KTH.

## English proficiency requirement
- English proficiency equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course **English 6 / English Level 2**.
- Can be met with an English test, e.g., an overall **IELTS score of 6.5** or a **TOEFL score of 4.5**.
- Depending on your country of previous studies you could also meet the requirement through completed upper secondary or university studies.
- Recognised English tests and country-specific applicability are specified via University Admissions.

## Specific requirements for Computer Science
- A bachelor's degree corresponding to **180 ECTS credits**, or equivalent, including courses in:

**Mathematics** — four different subjects with a total of **28.5 ECTS credits**. These subjects must include:
- a course in **Calculus in one variable**
- a course in **Linear Algebra**
- a course in **Probability Theory and Statistics**
- a course in **Discrete Mathematics**

**Computer technology / Computer science and engineering / Computer science / Information technology** — three different subjects with a total of **22.5 ECTS credits**. These subjects must include:
- a course in **Object Oriented Programming**
- a course in **Algorithms and Data Structures**
- an **in-depth course in Algorithmic Complexity**

## Track / specialisation applicability (in-program special-eligibility notes)
- Within the programme track, there may be courses with additional requirements for special qualifications, stated under the heading **"Special eligibility"** in the syllabus. Examples given:
  - **Multivariable analysis** is a special eligibility requirement for compulsory courses within the tracks **Data analysis** and **Cognitive systems**.
  - **Human-computer interaction** is a special entry requirement for compulsory courses within the **Interaction Design** track.
  - Additional prerequisites may exist for some conditionally elective or recommended courses within the tracks.
- (Context: these special-eligibility items are stated as syllabus-level/in-program conditions rather than pre-enrolment admission requirements.)

## Application documents — all must be submitted per University Admissions instructions
- Do not submit documents that are not requested.

**General documents:**
- **Degree certificates** — Official certificates of completed degrees. Documentation requirements vary by country (see University Admissions).
- **Transcript** — Official transcript of courses and grades completed in your degree. Students from Swedish universities that use **Ladok** do not need to submit degree certificates or transcripts (see University Admissions).
- **Proof of English proficiency** — depends on whether met by test or previous studies (see University Admissions).
- **Identification** — a copy of passport with personal data and photograph, or other identification document.

**Programme documents:**
- **CV** — KTH does not require a standard template, but the CV should clearly and concisely outline your education, relevant research or work experience, extracurricular activities, qualifications and achievements (awards, publications, expertise knowledge and skills, etc.). It **must be written in English**.
- **Letter of motivation** — explains why you chose this programme at KTH, what you hope to gain, and how your interests and skills will help you succeed. Include an autobiography with the development and relevance of your academic and professional pursuits, extracurricular activities and related experiences. KTH does not require a standard template, but it **must be in English and less than 500 words**. If applying to multiple programmes requiring a letter of motivation, submit one for each and **state which programme each letter applies to at the top of the page**.
- **Letters of recommendation** — **Two** letters of recommendation describing why you are the right choice for admission. Preferably, one referee from an academic environment and one from a professional setting. If applying for multiple programmes at KTH that request letters of recommendation, you may use the same letters for several programmes. You must provide an **English translation** if the letters are in a different language. The letters must have the referees' **full contact details**. If a referee wants to submit the letter themselves, they must **send it by post to University Admissions** and state your name and application number. **They cannot submit the letter via email.**

## Summary sheet (programme document)
- Submit the **summary sheet for Computer Science** via the link **when the application opens** — **do not upload it to your application on universityadmissions.se**.
- If you do not submit a **complete** summary sheet, it will **negatively affect your evaluation score**.
- Fill out all required information before submitting the form. For questions, contact the programme coordinator directly.

## Selection criteria
- Selection is based on: **study results** (grades from previous studies), **motivation for the studies** (awards, prizes and publications), and **previous education**.
- Prior education is evaluated on the quality and suitability of the subjects relevant to the programme. For **international** prior education, **university ranking is also part of the merit rating**.
- The merit rating is carried out on a **scale of 1–75**.

## Acceptance rate (2026 data — most recent stated on the page)
- Acceptance rate for the master's programme in Computer Science for **2026** was **8%**.
- **63 students admitted** out of the **762 applicants** who met the admission requirements.
- Advice given: to increase chances, select more than one programme when applying; you can apply for **up to four programmes** and rank them in order of preference.

## Recognition of prior learning
- If you entirely or partially lack a formal requirement for a course or programme but believe you have the necessary knowledge, you can apply for **recognition of prior learning**.

- a course in **Algorithms and Data Structures**

- Within the programme track, there may be courses with additional requirements for special qualifications, stated under the heading **"Special eligibility"** in the syllabus. Examples given:

- Do not submit documents that are not requested.

- **Degree certificates** — Official certificates of completed degrees. Documentation requirements vary by country (see University Admissions).

- **Identification** — a copy of passport with personal data and photograph, or other identification document.

requirements.requirement: Applicants must hold academic qualifications from an internationally recognised university equivalent to a Swedish bachelor's degree. Students in the final year of their bachelor's studies can meet the requirement. Students at universities abroad must submit documents according to University Admissions instructions. Students at Swedish universities must have completed 150 credits in their programme by 1 February.

requirements.requirement: English proficiency equivalent to Swedish upper secondary course English 6 / English Level 2 is required.
